decisions.choice: the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadrezzar: 605 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim became king in 609 BC, so his fourth year was 605 BC. That was the year Nebuchadrezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish (46:2, dated to the same year) and succeeded his father as king of Babylon. This is the first time Jeremiah dates a message by a foreign king's reign: from now on Babylon sets the calendar for Judah. The same year is the setting of chapter 36 (36:1) and of chapter 45. Daniel 1:1 speaks of the third year of Jehoiakim for Nebuchadnezzar's first move against Jerusalem; that probably counts Jehoiakim's years from his first full year rather than from his accession. The Greek translation lacks the words "that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar" (see the note at 1:1; this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the word ... concerning all the people of Judah: a message about them and addressed to them
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a message about the whole people; verse 2 adds that Jeremiah spoke it to them. It is the summing up of his preaching up to this point (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name with r, kept as the Hebrew has it here
decisions.reason: Jeremiah and Ezekiel mostly spell the king's name Nebuchadrezzar, close to the Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur ("Nabu, protect my heir"). Kings, Chronicles, Daniel and a few places in Jeremiah (27-29) spell it Nebuchadnezzar. Both name the same king, who reigned 605-562 BC.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: Each verse keeps the form of the name its Hebrew uses, so readers can see the two spellings; m3 explains that they are one man.

decisions.choice: a parenthesis (Literal); a relative clause (Balanced); a separate sentence (Readable); a comma at the end of the verse (Literal)
decisions.reason: The second date explains the first. The sentence runs on into verse 2, so Literal ends with a comma; Balanced and Readable finish the date here and let verse 2 begin a new sentence. Balanced uses the book's heading wording ("This message came to Jeremiah") and the dating formula "in the fourth year of the reign of", and Readable says plainly that the LORD gave the message.

decisions.choice: en el año cuarto de X (Literal); en el cuarto año del reinado de X (Balanced); en el cuarto año en que X era rey (Readable)
decisions.reason: The dated headings of Jeremiah keep this pattern at each level through the block, as the English note sets for "in the Nth year of X".

decisions.reason: The French wording of Jeremiah's dated headings for Jeremiah 18-34, following the English pattern by level and the Kings note's regnal formulas.

decisions.reason: The terms note's pattern for Jeremiah's dated headings at each level, after the regnal formulas of Kings.

decisions.choice: "여호야김의 제4년" (L); "여호야김이 다스린 지 4년째 되는 해" (B); "여호야김이 왕이 된 지 4년째 되는 해" (R)

records.literal_gloss: From thirteen year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, and until the day this, this three and twenty year[s] has come [the] word of Yahweh to me, and I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and not you have listened.

en.L: "From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day, these twenty-three years, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not listened.
en.B: "For twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, up to this very day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has come to me. Again and again I have spoken to you, but you have not listened.
en.R: "For twenty-three years {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been giving me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messages. It began in the thirteenth year that Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, and it has gone on until today. I have told you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messages over and over, but you have not listened.

es.L: «Desde el año trece de Josías hijo de Amón, rey de Judá, hasta este día, estos veintitrés años, ha venido a mí la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado, madrugando y hablando, y no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado.
es.B: «Durante veintitrés años, desde el año trece del reinado de Josías hijo de Amón, rey de Judá, hasta el día de hoy, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} ha venido a mí. Una y otra vez {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado, pero no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado.
es.R: «Durante veintitrés años {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha estado dando {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mensajes. Empezó en el año trece en que Josías hijo de Amón era rey de Judá, y ha seguido hasta hoy. Una y otra vez {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mensajes, pero no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado.

fr.L: « Depuis la treizième année de Josias fils d’Amon, roi de Juda, jusqu’à ce jour, voici vingt-trois ans que la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} m’est adressée, et je vous ai parlé, me levant de bonne heure et parlant, et vous n’avez pas écouté.
fr.B: « Depuis vingt-trois ans, depuis la treizième année du règne de Josias fils d’Amon, roi de Juda, jusqu’à aujourd’hui, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} m’a été adressée. Je vous ai parlé sans relâche, mais vous n’avez pas écouté.
fr.R: « Depuis vingt-trois ans, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me donne {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} messages. Cela a commencé la treizième année où Josias, fils d’Amon, était roi de Juda, et cela a continué jusqu’à aujourd’hui. Je vous ai transmis {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} messages encore et encore, mais vous n’avez pas écouté.

sw.L: "Tangu mwaka wa kumi na tatu wa Yosia mwana wa Amoni, mfalme wa Yuda, mpaka siku hii ya leo, miaka hii ishirini na mitatu, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} limekuwa likinijia, nami nimesema nanyi, nikiamka mapema na kusema, lakini hamkusikiliza.

Nimewaambia ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mara nyingi sana, lakini hamkusikiliza.

vi.L: "Từ năm thứ mười ba đời Giô-si-a con trai A-môn, vua Giu-đa, cho đến ngày nay, đã hai mươi ba năm nay lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với tôi, và tôi đã nói với các người, dậy sớm mà nói, nhưng các người không nghe.
vi.B: "Đã hai mươi ba năm nay, từ năm thứ mười ba triều Giô-si-a con trai A-môn, vua Giu-đa, cho đến chính ngày hôm nay, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} vẫn đến với tôi. Tôi đã nói với các người hết lần này đến lần khác, nhưng các người không nghe.
vi.R: "Đã hai mươi ba năm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban sứ điệp của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho tôi. Việc ấy bắt đầu từ năm thứ mười ba Giô-si-a con trai A-môn làm vua Giu-đa và kéo dài cho đến hôm nay. Tôi đã nhiều lần nói cho các người biết sứ điệp của Ngài, nhưng các người không nghe.

ko.L: "유다 왕 아몬의 아들 요시야의 제13년부터 오늘까지, 이 23년 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임했고, 나는 너희에게 일찍 일어나 말하며 전했으나 너희는 듣지 않았다.
ko.B: "아몬의 아들 요시야가 유다를 다스린 지 13년째 되는 해부터 바로 오늘까지, 23년 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임했다. 나는 너희에게 거듭거듭 말했지만, 너희는 듣지 않았다.
ko.R: "23년 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀을 주셨다. 그 일은 아몬의 아들 요시야가 유다의 왕이 된 지 13년째 되는 해에 시작되어 오늘까지 계속되었다. 나는 너희에게 그분의 말씀을 몇 번이고 전했다. 그러나 너희는 듣지 않았다.

decisions.choice: twenty-three years: from 627 BC to 605 BC, counting both the first and the last year
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's call came in Josiah's thirteenth year (1:2). Josiah reigned thirty-one years (2 Kings 22:1), which leaves nineteen years of his reign; Jehoahaz reigned three months, and this is Jehoiakim's fourth year (verse 1). Counted the ancient way, with the first and last years both included, that gives twenty-three years.

decisions.choice: rising early and speaking: speaking again and again, without giving up
decisions.reason: As in 7:13. The form of the first verb here is unusual (it looks like an Aramaic spelling), but the phrase is the one Jeremiah uses throughout for God's untiring warnings.

decisions.choice: I have spoken ... you have not listened: the prophet's whole ministry summed up as one long appeal refused
decisions.reason: The perfect verbs look back over the whole twenty-three years. Verse 4 sets the LORD's sending of all his prophets beside Jeremiah's own preaching.

decisions.choice: rising early and speaking (L); again and again (B); over and over (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: giving me his messages ... told you his messages
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "the word of the LORD came to me" means (as at 1:2), and that what Jeremiah spoke was that message.

decisions.choice: madrugando y hablando (Literal); una y otra vez (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The idiom of rising early keeps the wording the terms note sets for the block (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: nikiamka mapema na kusema (Literal); tena na tena (Balanced); mara nyingi sana (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili for Jeremiah's "rising early and speaking" at each level.

decisions.choice: "me levant de bonne heure et parlant" (L); "sans relâche" (B); "encore et encore" (R)
decisions.reason: The French wording the terms note sets for this phrase throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for "rising early and speaking", used each time it returns in these chapters (verse 4; 26:5; 29:19; 32:33).

decisions.reason: The prophet rebuking the people says "các người" (terms note); God's own words quoted inside (verses 5-7) keep his "các ngươi".

decisions.reason: The terms note's forms for "rising early and speaking" in Jeremiah (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to the people in the plain style ("너희", "듣지 않았다")
decisions.reason: A prophet's sermon to the people, as in 19:14-15; God is spoken of with the honorific.

source.text: וְשָׁלַח֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֲלֵיכֶ֜ם אֶֽת־כָּל־עֲבָדָ֧יו הַנְּבִאִ֛ים הַשְׁכֵּ֥ם וְשָׁלֹ֖חַ וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־הִטִּיתֶ֥ם אֶֽת־אָזְנְכֶ֖ם לִשְׁמֹֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Yahweh to you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending, and not you listened, and not you inclined your ear to hear,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent to you all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets, rising early and sending [them], but you have not listened, nor have you inclined your ear to hear,
en.B: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent you all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets again and again, but you have not listened or even paid attention.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has also sent you all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets, over and over. But you would not listen. You would not even pay attention.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha enviado a todos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos los profetas, madrugando y enviando[los], pero no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado, ni {{plural_you:han|habéis}} inclinado {{plural_you:su oído|vuestro oído}} para oír,
es.B: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha enviado una y otra vez a todos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos los profetas, pero no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado ni {{plural_you:han|habéis}} prestado atención.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} también {{plural_you:les|os}} ha enviado a todos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos los profetas, una y otra vez. Pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} escuchar. Ni siquiera {{plural_you:prestaron|prestasteis}} atención.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a envoyé tous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs les prophètes, se levant de bonne heure et [les] envoyant, mais vous n’avez pas écouté, et vous n’avez pas tendu l’oreille pour entendre,
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a envoyé sans relâche tous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs les prophètes, mais vous n’avez pas écouté, vous n’avez même pas prêté attention.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a aussi envoyé tous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs les prophètes, encore et encore. Mais vous n’avez pas voulu écouter. Vous n’avez même pas fait attention.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatumia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote manabii, akiamka mapema na kuwatuma, lakini hamkusikiliza, wala hamkutega sikio lenu kusikia,
sw.B: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatumia tena na tena watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote, manabii, lakini hamkusikiliza wala hata kujali.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatumia pia mara nyingi sana watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote, manabii. Lakini hamkutaka kusikiliza. Hata hamkujali.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai đến với các người mọi đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri, dậy sớm mà sai [họ] đến, nhưng các người không nghe, cũng không nghiêng tai để nghe,
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cũng đã sai mọi đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri đến với các người hết lần này đến lần khác, nhưng các người không nghe, cũng chẳng thèm lắng tai.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cũng đã nhiều lần sai mọi đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri đến với các người. Nhưng các người không chịu nghe. Các người cũng chẳng thèm để ý.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 모든 종 예언자들을 너희에게 일찍 일어나 보내셨으나, 너희는 듣지 않았고 귀를 기울여 듣지도 않았다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 종 예언자들을 모두 너희에게 거듭거듭 보내셨으나, 너희는 듣지 않았고 귀를 기울이지도 않았다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분의 종 예언자들도 모두 너희에게 몇 번이고 보내셨다. 그러나 너희는 듣지 않았다. 귀를 기울이지도 않았다.

decisions.choice: his servants the prophets: those who served God by bringing his word
decisions.reason: As in 7:25. Jeremiah was not alone: the LORD had sent prophet after prophet with the same call (2 Kings 17:13).

decisions.choice: rising early and sending: sending them constantly
decisions.reason: As in 7:25.

decisions.choice: you did not incline your ear: you did not even turn to listen
decisions.reason: To bend the ear toward someone is to give attention. The people refused even the first step of hearing (7:24, 26; 11:8).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: As in 7:25, "servant" is kept at every level when the word names those who serve God.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending (L); again and again (B); over and over (R); inclined your ear (L); paid attention (B, R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for the first phrase; Balanced and Readable give the sense of the ear idiom. The Literal sentence runs on into verse 5 and ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: siervos
decisions.reason: God's servants the prophets are "siervos" at every level, as the terms note sets for the servant of the LORD.

decisions.choice: watumishi wake manabii
decisions.reason: God's servants the prophets are "watumishi" at every level, never "watumwa", as the terms note sets for the servant of the LORD.

decisions.choice: "serviteurs" at every level
decisions.reason: As the Kings note sets for God's named servants in French: "serviteur" at every level, Literal included.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" (servants)
decisions.reason: God's servants the prophets are "đầy tớ" at every level, Literal included, as the terms note settles; "nô lệ" is kept for slavery itself (34:8-22).

decisions.choice: "종" for God's servants the prophets
decisions.reason: As the terms note: "종" at every level, never "노예".

source.text: לֵאמֹ֗ר שֽׁוּבוּ־נָ֞א אִ֣ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֤וֹ הָֽרָעָה֙ וּמֵרֹ֣עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּשְׁבוּ֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם וְלַאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לְמִן־עוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: saying: Turn please each from his way the evil and from [the] evil of your deeds, and dwell on the land which gave Yahweh to you and to your fathers from of old and until forever.

en.L: saying, 'Turn now, each one from {{gender:their|his}} evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and dwell in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to you and to your fathers from of old and forever.
en.B: They said, 'Turn back, every one of you, from your evil ways and your evil deeds, and you will live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to you and your ancestors to keep for all time.
en.R: The prophets told you, 'Each of you must stop living in your evil ways and doing evil things. Then you can live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to you and to your ancestors, to be yours forever.

es.L: diciendo: “{{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} ahora cada uno de su mal camino y de la maldad de {{plural_you:sus obras|vuestras obras}}, y {{plural_you:habiten|habitad}} en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dio a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} desde antiguo y para siempre.
es.B: Ellos decían: “{{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de {{plural_you:sus malos caminos y de sus malas obras|vuestros malos caminos y de vuestras malas obras}}, y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}} en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dio a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} para siempre.
es.R: Los profetas {{plural_you:les|os}} decían: “Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe dejar de vivir en sus malos caminos y de hacer el mal. Entonces {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} vivir en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dio a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, para que fuera {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}} para siempre.

fr.L: disant : “Revenez donc, chacun de sa mauvaise voie et de la méchanceté de vos actions, et habitez sur la terre que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donnée, à vous et à vos pères, depuis toujours et pour toujours.
fr.B: Ils disaient : “Revenez, chacun de vous, de votre mauvaise conduite et de vos mauvaises actions, et vous habiterez le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donné, à vous et à vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, pour toujours.
fr.R: Les prophètes vous disaient : “Que chacun de vous abandonne sa mauvaise conduite et arrête de faire le mal. Alors vous pourrez habiter le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a donné, à vous et à vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, pour qu’il soit à vous pour toujours.

sw.L: wakisema, 'Rudini sasa, kila mmoja kutoka njia yake mbaya na kutoka uovu wa matendo yenu, mkae katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa ninyi na baba zenu tangu zamani hata milele.
sw.B: Walisema, 'Rudini, kila mmoja wenu, mziache njia zenu mbaya na matendo yenu maovu, nanyi mtakaa katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa ninyi na babu zenu iwe yenu daima.
sw.R: Manabii waliwaambia, 'Kila mmoja wenu na aache kuishi katika njia zake mbaya na kutenda maovu. Ndipo mtaweza kuishi katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa ninyi na babu zenu, iwe yenu milele.

vi.L: rằng: 'Mỗi người hãy quay lại khỏi đường ác của mình và khỏi điều ác trong việc làm của các ngươi, thì các ngươi sẽ ở trên đất mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho các ngươi và cho tổ phụ các ngươi từ xưa cho đến đời đời.
vi.B: Họ nói: 'Mỗi người trong các ngươi hãy quay lại khỏi đường lối gian ác và những việc làm xấu xa của mình, thì các ngươi sẽ được ở trên đất mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho các ngươi và tổ tiên các ngươi để giữ mãi mãi.
vi.R: Các nhà tiên tri đã bảo các người: 'Mỗi người trong các ngươi phải thôi sống theo đường lối gian ác và thôi làm điều ác. Khi ấy các ngươi sẽ được sống trên đất {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho các ngươi và tổ tiên các ngươi, để làm sản nghiệp đời đời.

ko.L: 그들이 말했다. '너희는 저마다 자기의 악한 길과 너희 행실의 악에서 돌아오너라. 그러면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 너희 조상들에게 예로부터 영원히 주신 그 땅에서 살 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 말했다. '너희는 모두 저마다 악한 길과 악한 행실에서 돌아오너라. 그러면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 너희 조상들에게 영원히 주신 땅에서 살게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 예언자들은 너희에게 말했다. '너희는 저마다 악하게 사는 길에서 돌아오너라. 악한 일을 그만두어라. 그러면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 너희 조상들에게 영원히 주신 땅에서 살 수 있을 것이다.

decisions.choice: turn: repent, come back from evil to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is Jeremiah's key word for repentance (3:12, 14, 22; 18:11). It means a turning of the whole life, here from evil ways and deeds.

decisions.choice: and dwell: the result promised to those who turn
decisions.reason: The second command follows the first as its outcome: turn, and you will live in the land. The same promise stands in the temple sermon (7:3, 7).

decisions.choice: from of old and forever: the land given for all time
decisions.reason: The double phrase covers the whole span from the gift to the ancestors on into the future, as in 7:7. The gift was lasting, but living in it depended on faithfulness.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the prophets' words, inside Jeremiah's speech
decisions.reason: Jeremiah quotes what the prophets said, so their words take single quotation marks. Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence and supply "They said" or "The prophets told you"; Readable also supplies "must" and "Then" to show that living in the land depended on turning. Literal follows 18:11 for "each one from their evil way", with the gender setting, since the call is to men and women alike.

decisions.choice: the prophets' message uses God's "các ngươi"
decisions.reason: The message the prophets brought is God's own word, in which he speaks as "Ta" (verse 6), so it takes God's address to the people.

decisions.choice: Verses 4-5 closed as separate sentences
decisions.reason: Korean cannot place a quotation's verb before verse 5's marker, so verse 4 ends and verse 5 opens with "그들이 말했다"; the prophets' words take single quotation marks inside Jeremiah's speech.

source.text: וְאַל־תֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְעָבְדָ֖ם וּלְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־תַכְעִ֤יסוּ אוֹתִי֙ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א אָרַ֖ע לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not go after gods other to serve them and to bow down to them, and not provoke me with [the] work of your hands, and not I will do harm to you.

en.L: And do not go after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them, and do not provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with the work of your hands; then I will do you no harm.'
en.B: Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them. Do not make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with the idols your hands have made, and I will not harm you.'
en.R: Do not follow other gods. Do not serve them or bow down to worship them. Do not make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry by worshiping idols you have made with your own hands. If you obey, I will not punish you.'

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} tras otros dioses para servirles y postrarse ante ellos, y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:provoquen|provoquéis}} a ira con la obra de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}; y no {{plural_you:les|os}} haré mal”.
es.B: No {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} a otros dioses para servirles y adorarlos. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} enojar con los ídolos que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} con {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, y no {{plural_you:les|os}} haré daño”.
es.R: No {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} a otros dioses. No les {{plural_you:sirvan|sirváis}} ni {{plural_you:se inclinen|os inclinéis}} para adorarlos. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} enojar adorando ídolos que {{plural_you:ustedes mismos han|vosotros mismos habéis}} hecho con {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}. Si {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}}, no {{plural_you:los|os}} castigaré”.

fr.L: Et n’allez pas après d’autres dieux pour les servir et vous prosterner devant eux, et ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}irritez pas par l’œuvre de vos mains ; alors je ne vous ferai pas de mal.”
fr.B: Ne suivez pas d’autres dieux pour les servir et les adorer. Ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}irritez pas par les idoles que vos mains ont faites, et je ne vous ferai pas de mal.”
fr.R: Ne suivez pas d’autres dieux. Ne les servez pas et ne vous prosternez pas devant eux pour les adorer. Ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mettez pas en colère en adorant des idoles que vous avez faites de vos propres mains. Si vous obéissez, je ne vous punirai pas.”

sw.L: Wala msiifuate miungu mingine ili kuitumikia na kuisujudia, wala msinikasirishe kwa kazi ya mikono yenu; nami sitawadhuru.'
sw.B: Msiifuate miungu mingine ili kuitumikia na kuiabudu. Msinikasirishe kwa sanamu mlizozitengeneza kwa mikono yenu, nami sitawadhuru.'
sw.R: Msiifuate miungu mingine. Msiitumikie wala msiisujudie kuiabudu. Msinikasirishe kwa kuabudu sanamu mlizotengeneza kwa mikono yenu wenyewe. Mkitii, sitawaadhibu.'

vi.L: Đừng đi theo các thần khác để phục vụ và quỳ lạy chúng, đừng chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng công việc tay các ngươi làm; thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không làm hại các ngươi.'
vi.B: Đừng đi theo các thần khác để phục vụ và thờ lạy chúng. Đừng chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng những thần tượng do tay các ngươi làm ra, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không làm hại các ngươi.'
vi.R: Đừng đi theo các thần khác. Đừng phục vụ hay cúi lạy thờ chúng. Đừng chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng cách thờ những thần tượng do chính tay các ngươi làm ra. Nếu các ngươi vâng lời, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không phạt các ngươi.'

ko.L: 다른 신들을 따라가 그들을 섬기거나 그들에게 절하지 말고, 너희 손으로 만든 것으로 나를 노엽게 하지 마라. 그러면 내가 너희에게 해를 끼치지 않을 것이다.'
ko.B: 다른 신들을 따라가 섬기거나 경배하지 마라. 너희 손으로 만든 우상들로 나를 노엽게 하지 마라. 그러면 내가 너희를 해치지 않겠다.'
ko.R: 다른 신들을 따르지 마라. 그들을 섬기거나 그들에게 절하지 마라. 너희 손으로 만든 우상을 섬겨서 나를 화나게 하지 마라. 너희가 순종하면 내가 너희를 벌하지 않겠다.'

decisions.choice: go after other gods: give loyalty to other gods
decisions.reason: To go after someone is to follow them as one's master. The phrase comes from the covenant warnings (Deuteronomy 6:14; 8:19) and runs through Jeremiah (7:6, 9; 11:10).

decisions.choice: the work of your hands: idols made by human hands
decisions.reason: The phrase means the idols, things people make and then worship (1:16; Deuteronomy 4:28). It could also mean their deeds in general, but beside "other gods" the idols are meant.

decisions.choice: provoke me ... I will do you no harm: God speaks in his own voice inside the prophets' message
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke God's words in his name, so the message they gave says "me" and "I" of God.

decisions.choice: If you obey, I will not punish you
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "If you obey" to show the condition, and says "punish" for the harm God would bring as judgment.

decisions.choice: "나를", "내가" inside the prophets' message
decisions.reason: God speaks in his own voice within the prophets' message (meaning decision m3); Korean keeps the first person and God's plain style.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לְמַ֧עַן הַכְעִיסֵ֛נִי בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיכֶ֖ם לְרַ֥ע לָכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But not you have listened to me, declaration of Yahweh, so as to provoke me with [the] work of your hands to harm to you.

en.L: But you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that you have provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.
en.B: But you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with the idols your hands have made, and brought harm on yourselves.
en.R: But you would not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with the idols you made, and so you have brought trouble on yourselves.

es.L: Pero no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, de modo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:han|habéis}} provocado a ira con la obra de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, para {{plural_you:su propio mal|vuestro propio mal}}.
es.B: Pero no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho enojar con los ídolos que {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} con {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, y {{plural_you:se han|os habéis}} traído desgracia a {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}}.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} escucharme, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Me {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} enojar con los ídolos que {{plural_you:fabricaron|fabricasteis}}, y así {{plural_you:se han|os habéis}} buscado problemas.

fr.L: Mais vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas écouté, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, de sorte que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez irrité par l’œuvre de vos mains, pour votre malheur.
fr.B: Mais vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas écouté, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez irrité par les idoles que vos mains ont faites, et vous avez attiré le malheur sur vous.
fr.R: Mais vous n’avez pas voulu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écouter, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez mis en colère avec les idoles que vous avez fabriquées, et vous vous êtes ainsi attiré des malheurs.

sw.L: Lakini hamkunisikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hata mkanikasirisha kwa kazi ya mikono yenu, kwa madhara yenu wenyewe.
sw.B: Lakini hamkunisikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mmenikasirisha kwa sanamu mlizotengeneza kwa mikono yenu, mkajiletea madhara wenyewe.
sw.R: Lakini hamkutaka kunisikiliza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mlinikasirisha kwa sanamu mlizotengeneza, na hivyo mmejiletea taabu wenyewe.

vi.L: Nhưng các ngươi đã không nghe Ta, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, đến nỗi các ngươi đã chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng công việc tay các ngươi làm, chuốc lấy tai hại cho chính mình.
vi.B: Nhưng các ngươi đã không nghe Ta, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Các ngươi đã chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng những thần tượng do tay các ngươi làm ra, và chuốc lấy tai họa cho chính mình.
vi.R: Nhưng các ngươi không chịu nghe Ta, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Các ngươi đã chọc giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng những thần tượng do các ngươi làm ra, nên các ngươi đã tự chuốc lấy tai họa cho mình.

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 내 말을 듣지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 그래서 너희 손으로 만든 것으로 나를 노엽게 하여 너희 자신에게 해를 끼쳤다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 내 말을 듣지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 너희는 너희 손으로 만든 우상들로 나를 노엽게 했고, 스스로 해를 불러들였다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 내 말을 듣지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 너희는 너희가 만든 우상들로 나를 화나게 했다. 그래서 너희 스스로 화를 불러들였다.

decisions.choice: you have not listened to me, declares the LORD: Jeremiah speaks God's words in God's own voice
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's report of his preaching turns into the LORD's own words, marked by "declares the LORD". There is no new quotation in the Hebrew; the prophet speaks for God.

decisions.choice: so that you provoked me ... to your harm: the result of their refusal, which turns back on themselves
decisions.reason: The word "so that" here marks what came of their actions, not their purpose. They angered God, and the harm fell on them. The Hebrew has a written form "so as to provoke me" with a marginal reading "they provoked me"; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: declares (L, B); says (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for this formula, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable break the verse into shorter sentences.

source.text: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת יַ֕עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־דְּבָרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts: Because that not you have listened to my words,

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Because you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words,
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Because you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words,
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: You have not listened to what I said.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: Por cuanto no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} escuchado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras,

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Parce que vous n’avez pas écouté {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles,

sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Hamkusikiliza yale niliyosema.

ko.L: 그러므로 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희가 내 말을 듣지 않았으므로,

decisions.choice: therefore: the judgment that follows from twenty-three years of refusal
decisions.reason: The word links the sentence of judgment (verses 8-11) to the refusal described in verses 3-7. Inside Jeremiah's speech the LORD's words now follow directly.

decisions.choice: listened to: obeyed
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's words is to do what they say. The same verb runs through verses 3, 4 and 7.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts" (see Isaiah 1:9).

decisions.choice: a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Readable makes the reason its own sentence; verse 9 then states what God will do. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew sentence running into verse 9.

records.literal_gloss: here I [am] sending and I will take all [the] clans of [the] north, declaration of Yahweh, and to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon my servant, and I will bring them on the land this and on its inhabitants and on all the nations these around, and I will devote them to destruction and I will make them into a horror and into a hissing and into ruins of forever.

en.L: look, I am sending and I will take all the clans of the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and [I am sending] to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, and I will bring them against this land and against its inhabitants and against all these nations around [it]; and I will devote them to destruction, and I will make them a horror and a hissing and everlasting ruins.
en.B: I am going to send for all the peoples of the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I will bring them against this land and its people and against all the nations around it. I will devote them to destruction and make them a horror, an object of scorn, and ruins forever.
en.R: I am going to send for all the peoples from the north, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will send for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. I will bring them to attack this land and the people who live here, and all the nations around you. I will destroy them all completely. People will be horrified at them and mock them. Those places will lie in ruins forever.

es.B: Voy a mandar a buscar a todos los pueblos del norte, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo. Los traeré contra esta tierra y sus habitantes, y contra todas las naciones que la rodean. Los destinaré a la destrucción y haré de ellos un horror, un objeto de burla y ruinas para siempre.
es.R: Voy a mandar a buscar a todos los pueblos del norte, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Mandaré a buscar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia. Los traeré para que ataquen esta tierra y a la gente que vive aquí, y a todas las naciones que {{plural_you:los|os}} rodean. Los destruiré a todos por completo. La gente se horrorizará al verlos y se burlará de ellos. Esos lugares quedarán en ruinas para siempre.

fr.R: Je vais faire venir tous les peuples du nord, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je ferai venir {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone. Je les amènerai pour attaquer ce pays et ceux qui y habitent, et toutes les nations qui vous entourent. Je les détruirai complètement. Les gens seront horrifiés en les voyant et se moqueront d’eux. Ces lieux resteront en ruines pour toujours.

ko.L: 보아라, 내가 북쪽의 모든 족속과 내 종 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살을 불러 데려오겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 내가 그들을 이 땅과 그 주민들과 주변의 이 모든 민족에게 오게 하여, 그들을 진멸하고, 공포와 휘파람거리와 영원한 폐허가 되게 하겠다.
ko.B: 내가 북쪽의 모든 민족과 내 종 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살을 불러오겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 그들을 이 땅과 이 땅의 주민들과 주변의 모든 민족에게 쳐들어오게 하겠다. 내가 그 민족들을 진멸하여 공포의 대상과 비웃음거리와 영원한 폐허가 되게 하겠다.
ko.R: 내가 북쪽의 모든 민족을 불러오겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내 종 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살도 불러오겠다. 내가 그들이 이 땅과 이 땅에 사는 사람들과 주변의 모든 민족을 치게 하겠다. 내가 그들을 모두 완전히 멸망시키겠다. 사람들은 그들을 보고 몸서리치며 비웃을 것이다. 그곳들은 영원히 폐허로 남을 것이다.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar ... my servant: the foreign king is God's instrument, carrying out God's purpose
alternatives: my servant meaning a worshiper of God
decisions.reason: God calls the king of Babylon "my servant" here and in 27:6 and 43:10. The title does not mean that Nebuchadrezzar worshiped Israel's God or was good. It means that he did God's work, the way a servant carries out his master's orders: he would bring the judgment God had decreed. Isaiah says something similar of Assyria as the rod of God's anger (Isaiah 10:5-7) and of Cyrus as God's anointed (Isaiah 45:1). The title also tells Judah that resisting Babylon is resisting God (27:6-8). The Greek translation lacks "Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon my servant" here (see the note at 1:1; this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: all the clans of the north: the peoples who make up the army from the north
decisions.reason: The enemy from the north was announced in Jeremiah's call (1:14-15, where the same clans are named) and in the poems of chapters 4-6 (4:6; 6:22). Here, for the first time, that enemy is named: Babylon and its allies.

decisions.choice: devote them to destruction: give them over wholly to destruction as under God's ban
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the ban, the total destruction of what is given over to God (Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:21). What Israel once did to the nations of Canaan God now does to Judah and its neighbors.

decisions.choice: a horror and a hissing: a sight that appalls, at which people whistle in shock and scorn
decisions.reason: As in 19:8. Hissing or whistling at a ruin showed shock and contempt (18:16; 1 Kings 9:8). "Everlasting ruins" means ruins that will stand for a very long time.

decisions.choice: servant (every level)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "slave" at Literal for this word. Here, as in Isaiah, the word names one who carries out God's purpose (see m1), and Jeremiah uses the same title for God's prophets (verse 4), so "servant" is kept at every level. "Slave" would suggest that the point is the king's lowly status, when the point is the task God has given him.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction (L, B), destroy completely (R); a horror and a hissing (L), a horror, an object of scorn (B), horrified ... mock (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for the ban and for this list. Readable spells the list out in short sentences. Literal supplies "[I am sending]" and "[it]", which the Hebrew leaves understood.

decisions.choice: mi siervo
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar is God's "siervo" at every level, the same word as for the prophets, so the reader sees that the foreign king serves God's purpose (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los consagraré al exterminio (Literal); los destinaré a la destrucción (Balanced)
decisions.reason: *Herem* is giving over wholly to destruction under God's ban (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps the sense of consecration, Readable says "destruiré por completo".

decisions.choice: mtumishi wangu
decisions.reason: Nebukadreza is God's "mtumishi" at every level, as the English keeps "servant": the word says whose purpose he carries out (meaning decision m1). No deity span is used for him.

decisions.choice: "vouer à l'interdit" (L, B); "détruire complètement" (R)
decisions.reason: The ban (herem) as the published French books say it ("vouer à l'interdit"); Readable says what it means, as the English does. "Mon serviteur" for Nebuchadnezzar keeps "serviteur" at every level.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ Ta" for Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: The terms note's rule: God's servants are "đầy tớ" at every level, including Nebuchadrezzar "my servant" (25:9; 27:6), whom God uses as his instrument.

decisions.choice: "내 종 ... 느부갓레살"
decisions.reason: God calls the foreign king "my servant" (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps "종", the word used for God's servants the prophets, so the point is not lost.

decisions.choice: "진멸하다" for *heherim*
decisions.reason: "진멸" is the word for devoting to complete destruction under God's ban (meaning decision m3); Readable says "완전히 멸망시키다".

source.text: וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֣י מֵהֶ֗ם ק֤וֹל שָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חָתָ֖ן וְק֣וֹל כַּלָּ֑ה ק֥וֹל רֵחַ֖יִם וְא֥וֹר נֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make perish from them [the] sound of joy and [the] sound of gladness, [the] voice of bridegroom and [the] voice of bride, [the] sound of millstones and [the] light of lamp.

en.L: And I will banish from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
en.B: I will take away from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, the grinding of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
en.R: I will end the sounds of joy and happiness among them. No one will hear the happy voices of a bride and groom at their wedding. No one will hear the sound of grain being ground at the mill. No one will see the light of a lamp in their homes.

es.L: Y haré desaparecer de entre ellos la voz de gozo y la voz de alegría, la voz del novio y la voz de la novia, el ruido del molino y la luz de la lámpara.
es.B: Quitaré de en medio de ellos los sonidos de gozo y de alegría, las voces del novio y de la novia, el ruido de las piedras de moler y la luz de la lámpara.
es.R: Acabaré con los sonidos de gozo y felicidad entre ellos. Nadie oirá las voces alegres de los novios en su boda. Nadie oirá el ruido del grano al molerse en el molino. Nadie verá la luz de una lámpara en sus casas.

fr.L: Et je ferai disparaître du milieu d’eux le cri de joie et le cri d’allégresse, la voix du fiancé et la voix de la fiancée, le bruit des meules et la lumière de la lampe.
fr.B: Je ferai cesser chez eux les cris de joie et d’allégresse, les voix du fiancé et de la fiancée, le bruit des meules et la lumière de la lampe.
fr.R: Je ferai cesser chez eux les cris de joie et de bonheur. On n’entendra plus les voix joyeuses des mariés à leur mariage. On n’entendra plus le bruit du grain qu’on moud. On ne verra plus la lumière des lampes dans les maisons.

sw.L: Nami nitaondoa kwao sauti ya furaha na sauti ya shangwe, sauti ya bwana arusi na sauti ya bibi arusi, sauti ya mawe ya kusagia na nuru ya taa.
sw.B: Nitaziondoa kwao sauti za furaha na shangwe, sauti za bwana arusi na bibi arusi, mlio wa mawe ya kusagia na mwanga wa taa.
sw.R: Nitakomesha sauti za furaha na shangwe kati yao. Hakuna atakayesikia sauti za furaha za bibi arusi na bwana arusi harusini. Hakuna atakayesikia sauti ya nafaka ikisagwa kwa jiwe la kusagia. Hakuna atakayeona mwanga wa taa majumbani mwao.

vi.L: Ta sẽ làm cho tiêu mất khỏi giữa chúng tiếng vui mừng và tiếng hân hoan, tiếng chàng rể và tiếng cô dâu, tiếng cối xay và ánh sáng của đèn.
vi.B: Ta sẽ cất khỏi chúng tiếng vui mừng hân hoan, tiếng chàng rể và cô dâu, tiếng cối xay và ánh đèn.
vi.R: Ta sẽ chấm dứt những tiếng vui mừng hớn hở giữa chúng. Sẽ không ai còn nghe tiếng cười nói của cô dâu chú rể trong ngày cưới. Sẽ không ai còn nghe tiếng xay lúa nơi cối xay. Sẽ không ai còn thấy ánh đèn trong nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들에게서 기뻐하는 소리와 즐거워하는 소리, 신랑의 목소리와 신부의 목소리, 맷돌 소리와 등불 빛을 없애겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그들에게서 기뻐하고 즐거워하는 소리, 신랑과 신부의 목소리, 맷돌 가는 소리와 등불 빛을 사라지게 하겠다.
ko.R: 내가 그들 가운데서 기쁘고 즐거운 소리가 그치게 하겠다. 결혼식에서 신랑 신부의 즐거운 목소리도 들리지 않을 것이다. 맷돌로 곡식을 가는 소리도 들리지 않을 것이다. 집집마다 켜 두던 등불 빛도 보이지 않을 것이다.

decisions.choice: the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride: the joy of weddings, the sound of ordinary happy life
decisions.reason: As in 7:34 and 16:9. This verse adds two more signs of daily life to the list.

decisions.choice: the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp: daily bread and a lived-in home
decisions.reason: Every household ground its grain each morning with a pair of hand millstones, and a small oil lamp burned in the house at night. When both stop, no one is left to bake bread or keep a home. Revelation 18:22-23 takes up the same pictures for the fall of Babylon.

decisions.choice: I will make perish: I will put an end to these sounds completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or make vanish. 7:34 says "I will make cease" with another verb; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 for joy, gladness, bridegroom and bride
decisions.reason: The same list keeps the same words at each level as in 7:34. Readable explains the millstones (grain being ground) and says that the lamps are in their homes.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 for joy, gladness, bridegroom and bride
decisions.reason: The same Vietnamese words as the drafted 7:34 at each level, as the English keeps that verse's wording; 33:11 reverses them in the same words.

source.text: וְהָֽיְתָה֙ כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את לְחָרְבָּ֖ה לְשַׁמָּ֑ה וְעָ֨בְד֜וּ הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֛לֶּה אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will become all the land this a ruin, a horror, and will serve the nations these [the] king of Babylon seventy year[s].

en.L: And this whole land will become a ruin [and] a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
en.B: This whole land will become a desolate ruin, and for seventy years these nations will serve the king of Babylon.
en.R: This whole land will become an empty ruin, a terrible sight. These nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

es.L: Y toda esta tierra será una ruina [y] un horror, y estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia setenta años.
es.B: Toda esta tierra quedará convertida en una ruina desolada, y durante setenta años estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia.
es.R: Toda esta tierra se convertirá en una ruina vacía, algo horrible de ver. Estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia durante setenta años.

fr.L: Et tout ce pays deviendra une ruine [et] une horreur, et ces nations serviront le roi de Babylone soixante-dix ans.
fr.B: Tout ce pays deviendra une ruine désolée, et pendant soixante-dix ans ces nations serviront le roi de Babylone.
fr.R: Tout ce pays deviendra une ruine vide, un spectacle terrible. Ces nations seront au service du roi de Babylone pendant soixante-dix ans.

sw.L: Na nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu [na] kitisho, na mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli miaka sabini.
sw.B: Nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu matupu, na kwa miaka sabini mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli.
sw.R: Nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu matupu, mahali pa kutisha. Mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli kwa miaka sabini.

vi.L: Cả xứ này sẽ thành nơi hoang tàn [và] một điều kinh hoàng, và các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn bảy mươi năm.
vi.B: Cả xứ này sẽ thành một nơi hoang tàn đổ nát, và các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn trong bảy mươi năm.
vi.R: Cả xứ này sẽ thành một nơi đổ nát trống không, một cảnh tượng khủng khiếp. Các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn trong bảy mươi năm.

ko.L: 그리고 이 온 땅이 폐허와 공포가 될 것이고, 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.
ko.B: 이 온 땅은 황폐한 폐허가 될 것이고, 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.
ko.R: 이 온 땅은 텅 빈 폐허, 끔찍한 곳이 될 것이다. 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.

decisions.choice: seventy years: the full span set for Babylon's rule, after which God will act
alternatives: an exact count of seventy years
a round number for a lifetime
decisions.reason: Seventy years is a full lifetime (Psalm 90:10) and a round number for a complete period (Isaiah 23:15 says the same of Tyre). Babylon's rule over the region lasted from about 605 BC, the year of this message, until Babylon fell to Cyrus in 539 BC, close to seventy years. Others count from the temple's destruction in 586 BC to its rebuilding in 516 BC, exactly seventy. The number returns in 29:10, where it marks the time before the exiles return. 2 Chronicles 36:21 reads it as the land keeping its missed sabbaths (Leviticus 26:34-35), Zechariah 1:12 and 7:5 count it in their own day, and Daniel 9:2 tells of Daniel reading this prophecy and praying, with an answer that speaks of seventy weeks (Daniel 9:24). The text gives a set time; how its years were counted is not stated.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a horror: a desolate land that appalls those who see it
decisions.reason: The second word is the one translated "horror" in verse 9. Of a land it describes both the desolation and the shock of those who see it.

decisions.choice: these nations: Judah and the neighboring nations named in verse 9
decisions.reason: "These nations" points back to the nations around Judah in verse 9; Judah is included with them under Babylon.

decisions.choice: a desolate ruin (B); an empty ruin, a terrible sight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two nouns into one phrase; Readable keeps both ideas, the emptiness and the shock.

decisions.choice: setenta años
decisions.reason: The seventy years keep the published wording of 2 Chronicles 36:21 at every level.

decisions.choice: miaka sabini
decisions.reason: As 2 Chronicles 36:21, so the reader can see the number that Chronicles and Daniel take up.

decisions.choice: "soixante-dix ans"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: the French of France, never "septante", for the seventy years throughout.

decisions.choice: "bảy mươi năm"
decisions.reason: The seventy years, worded as in 2 Chronicles 36:21 (terms note), the same here and in 29:10.

decisions.choice: "70년", in figures at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note writes the seventy years in figures at every level, as 2 Chronicles 36:21.

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה כִמְלֹ֣אות שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֡ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד עַל־מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֩ וְעַל־הַגּ֨וֹי הַה֧וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־עֲוֺנָ֖ם וְעַל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ לְשִֽׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when are completed seventy year[s], I will visit on [the] king of Babylon and on the nation that, declaration of Yahweh, their iniquity, and on [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, and I will make it desolations of forever.

en.L: And it will be, when seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it an everlasting desolation.
en.B: But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will punish the land of the Chaldeans and make it a desolation forever.
en.R: But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and his nation for their sins, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will punish the land of the Babylonians and make it an empty waste forever.

es.L: Y sucederá que cuando se hayan cumplido los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a aquella nación, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por su iniquidad, y a la tierra de los caldeos, y la convertiré en desolación eterna.
es.B: Pero cuando se cumplan los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a aquella nación por su culpa, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Castigaré la tierra de los caldeos y la convertiré en una desolación para siempre.
es.R: Pero cuando se cumplan los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a su nación por sus pecados, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Castigaré la tierra de los babilonios y la convertiré en un desierto para siempre.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand les soixante-dix ans seront accomplis, que je punirai le roi de Babylone et cette nation, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, pour leur iniquité, ainsi que le pays des Chaldéens, et j’en ferai une désolation éternelle.
fr.B: Mais quand les soixante-dix ans seront passés, je punirai le roi de Babylone et cette nation pour leur faute, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je punirai le pays des Chaldéens et j’en ferai une désolation pour toujours.
fr.R: Mais quand les soixante-dix ans seront passés, je punirai le roi de Babylone et son peuple pour leurs péchés, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je punirai le pays des Babyloniens et j’en ferai un désert vide pour toujours.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, miaka sabini itakapotimia, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lile, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa uovu wao, na nchi ya Wakaldayo, nami nitaifanya kuwa ukiwa wa milele.
sw.B: Lakini miaka sabini itakapokwisha, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lile kwa hatia yao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitaiadhibu nchi ya Wakaldayo na kuifanya kuwa ukiwa milele.
sw.R: Lakini miaka sabini itakapokwisha, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lake kwa dhambi zao, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitaiadhibu nchi ya Wababeli na kuifanya kuwa nyika tupu milele.

vi.L: Khi bảy mươi năm đã mãn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, vì tội ác của chúng, cùng xứ của người Canh-đê, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho nó thành nơi hoang vu đời đời.
vi.B: Nhưng khi bảy mươi năm đã mãn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc ấy vì tội lỗi của chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Ta sẽ phạt xứ của người Canh-đê và làm cho nó thành nơi hoang vu mãi mãi.
vi.R: Nhưng khi bảy mươi năm đã qua, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc của vua ấy vì tội lỗi của chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ta sẽ phạt xứ của người Ba-by-lôn và làm cho nó thành một nơi hoang vắng mãi mãi.

ko.L: 그리고 70년이 차면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그 민족을 그들의 죄악 때문에 벌하고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다, 갈대아 사람들의 땅도 벌하여 그 땅을 영원한 황무지로 만들겠다.
ko.B: 그러나 70년이 다 차면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그 민족을 그들의 죄 때문에 벌하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 갈대아 사람들의 땅을 벌하여 영원히 황무지로 만들겠다.
ko.R: 그러나 70년이 끝나면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그의 나라를 그들이 지은 죄 때문에 벌하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 바빌로니아 사람들의 땅을 벌하여 영원히 텅 빈 땅으로 만들겠다.

decisions.choice: I will visit on ... their iniquity: I will punish them for their guilt
decisions.reason: To "visit" a sin on someone is to bring its punishment on them (5:9; Exodus 20:5). Babylon was God's instrument, but it would answer for its own cruelty and pride (50:29-32; 51:24).

decisions.choice: when seventy years are completed: the limit God has set to Babylon's rule
decisions.reason: See verse 11. The judgment on Judah has an end, and the nation that brought it will be judged in turn; chapters 50-51 spell this out.

decisions.choice: the land of the Chaldeans: Babylonia
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings ruled Babylon in Jeremiah's time, so the name stands for the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L), guilt (B), sins (R); Chaldeans (L, B), Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for these terms, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable repeat "I will punish" before the land to make the sentence clear.

source.text: וְהֵֽבֵאתִי֙ עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔יא אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֣רְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הַכָּתוּב֙ בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נִבָּ֥א יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring on the land that all my words which I have spoken against it, all the [thing] written in the book this, which prophesied Jeremiah against all the nations.

en.L: And I will bring on that land all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
en.B: I will bring on that land everything I have said against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
en.R: I will make everything I have said against Babylon come true. All of it is written in this book. It is what Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

es.L: Y traeré sobre esa tierra todas {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras que he hablado contra ella, todo lo que está escrito en este libro, lo que profetizó Jeremías contra todas las naciones.
es.B: Traeré sobre esa tierra todo lo que he dicho contra ella, todo lo que está escrito en este libro, lo que Jeremías profetizó contra todas las naciones.
es.R: Haré que se cumpla todo lo que he dicho contra Babilonia. Todo está escrito en este libro. Es lo que Jeremías profetizó contra todas las naciones.

fr.L: Et je ferai venir sur ce pays toutes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles que j’ai prononcées contre lui, tout ce qui est écrit dans ce livre, ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.
fr.B: Je ferai venir sur ce pays tout ce que j’ai annoncé contre lui, tout ce qui est écrit dans ce livre, ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.
fr.R: Je ferai arriver tout ce que j’ai annoncé contre Babylone. Tout cela est écrit dans ce livre. C’est ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.

sw.L: Nami nitaleta juu ya nchi ile maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote niliyoyanena juu yake, yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki, ambayo Yeremia alitabiri juu ya mataifa yote.
sw.B: Nitaleta juu ya nchi ile kila kitu nilichosema dhidi yake, yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki, ambayo Yeremia alitabiri dhidi ya mataifa yote.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew order, in which the oracles against the nations come later in the book (chapters 46-51)
alternatives: the Greek order, with the oracles against the nations following here
decisions.reason: This is the point at which the Greek translation of Jeremiah places its oracles against the nations, which the Hebrew gives as chapters 46-51. In the Greek, the words "which Jeremiah prophesied against the nations" serve as the heading of those oracles, and the Greek lacks verse 14. See the note at 1:1. This translation follows the Hebrew order. These statements come from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: which Jeremiah prophesied: words that speak of Jeremiah in the third person, inside God's speech
decisions.reason: God has been speaking in the first person ("my words"), and here Jeremiah is named as the one who prophesied. The clause reads like a note that describes the book, joined to God's words; it shows that the prophet's messages were already being gathered in writing (compare 36:2, 32, dated to the same year).

decisions.choice: that land: Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans in verse 12

decisions.choice: Babylon

decisions.choice: "예레미야가" named in the third person inside God's speech
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew (meaning decision m2), God's words speak of Jeremiah by name; Korean keeps it rather than turning it into "you".

decisions.choice: the cup of the wine of wrath: God's judgment pictured as a cup the nations must drink
decisions.reason: The cup that makes those who drink it reel is a common picture of God's judgment: Psalm 75:9; Isaiah 51:17, 22; Habakkuk 2:16; Lamentations 4:21; Ezekiel 23:31-33. Jeremiah returns to it in 49:12 and 51:7, where Babylon itself is the cup in God's hand. Revelation takes it up in the "wine of God's wrath" (Revelation 14:10; 16:19).

decisions.choice: the wine, the wrath: wine that is God's wrath
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand side by side, "the wine, the wrath". The second explains the first: the wine is God's anger. It is not wine poured out because of wrath, but wrath itself given as drink.

decisions.choice: take ... and make them drink: a prophetic sign, whose manner is not described
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Jeremiah carried a cup to the kings of all these nations, saw it in a vision, or acted it out in Jerusalem before their envoys (compare 27:2-3). What matters is that his word carries God's judgment to the nations, as his call said (1:10).

decisions.choice: filled with the wine of my wrath (B); the wine is my anger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "my" because the cup is from God's hand and the wrath is his. Readable unfolds the picture in short sentences. The LORD's words to Jeremiah open a quotation that closes at the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: la copa del vino de la ira
decisions.reason: God's judgment pictured as a cup (meaning decision m1) is "copa" at every level, the everyday Spanish word for a drinking cup.

decisions.choice: kikombe cha divai ya ghadhabu
decisions.reason: "Kikombe" as the cup of judgment, the word the New Testament uses for the cup Jesus must drink (Matthew 26:39), so the picture is recognisable.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi me parla le SEIGNEUR" (L); "Le SEIGNEUR me dit ceci" (B); "Voici ce que le SEIGNEUR m'a dit" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula in Jeremiah's own narrative frame, as the terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: "chén rượu thịnh nộ"
decisions.reason: "Chén" is the cup of judgment and of the Lord's Supper in the published New Testament, so the picture of meaning decision m1 keeps its familiar word.

decisions.choice: "진노의 포도주가 담긴 잔"
decisions.reason: God's judgment as a cup of wine the nations must drink (meaning decision m1); "진노" is the word for God's wrath used in this book.

decisions.choice: reel and act madly: stagger and lose control, like drunken people

decisions.reason: The drunkenness stands for the effect of the war God sends: armies broken and peoples in panic. Verse 27 repeats the phrase.

decisions.choice: war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "the sword", as the set wording for sword, famine and pestilence does in Jeremiah.

ko.B: 그래서 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손에서 그 잔을 받아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 모든 민족에게 그것을 마시게 했다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 그 잔을 받았다. 그리고 그분께서 나를 보내신 모든 민족에게 그것을 마시게 했다. 그것을 마신 이들은 다음과 같다.

decisions.choice: I took ... and made them drink: Jeremiah does as he is told
decisions.reason: The account uses the same verbs as the command in verse 15. The list of those who drank follows in verses 18-26, one long sentence.

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse, with the list in verses 18-26
decisions.reason: The list of nations is the object of "made ... drink". Literal and Balanced end each verse of the list with a comma or semicolon; Readable supplies "These are the ones who drank it" and gives each group a short sentence.

decisions.choice: Verse 17 closed as a sentence, and the list of verses 18-26 set as a series of noun phrases
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last; a single sentence would have to hold its verb back to verse 26. The list is set as Korean sets a roll of names, each verse ending in a comma, as in the English Literal and Balanced; Readable makes each verse a sentence, as the English Readable does.

fr.B: Jérusalem et les villes de Juda, ses rois et ses chefs, pour en faire une ruine, un objet d’horreur et de moquerie, et une malédiction, comme on le voit aujourd’hui ;
fr.R: Jérusalem et les villes de Juda en ont bu, avec leurs rois et leurs chefs. Cela en a fait une ruine, une horreur, quelque chose dont les gens se moquent et une malédiction, comme on le voit aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Yerusalemu na miji ya Yuda, na wafalme wake [na] wakuu wake, ili kuwafanya kuwa magofu, kitisho, [kitu cha] kuzomewa na laana, kama [ilivyo] siku hii ya leo;

vi.L: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa, các vua [và] các quan trưởng của nó, để làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một điều kinh hoàng, một tiếng huýt sáo và một sự rủa sả, như [hiện có] ngày nay;
vi.B: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa, các vua và các quan chức của nó, để làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một điều kinh hoàng, một mối nhạo báng và một lời nguyền rủa, như ngày nay;
vi.R: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa đã uống, cùng với các vua và các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng. Chén ấy làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một nơi đáng sợ, một chỗ người ta chế giễu và một lời nguyền rủa, như chúng ngày nay.

ko.L: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들과 그 왕들과 그 고관들, 곧 그들을 폐허와 공포와 휘파람거리와 저주가 되게 하려는 것이니, 오늘과 같다.
ko.B: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들과 그 왕들과 관리들이다. 그들을 폐허와 공포의 대상과 비웃음거리와 저주거리가 되게 하려는 것이니, 오늘 보는 바와 같다.
ko.R: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들이 왕들과 지도자들과 함께 그것을 마셨다. 그래서 그들은 오늘처럼 폐허가 되고, 끔찍한 곳, 사람들이 비웃는 곳, 저주받은 곳이 되었다.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem first: judgment begins with God's own city
decisions.reason: The list starts with Jerusalem and Judah before it turns to the nations. Verse 29 gives the reason: if God begins with the city called by his name, the other nations cannot escape.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse: a place destroyed, appalling, mocked and used as an example in curses
decisions.reason: As in verse 9 and 19:8. To become "a curse" is for one's name to be used when people curse, as in "may you be like them" (24:9; 29:22).

decisions.choice: as it is this day: the words look back on the judgment as already come
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the ruin had happened by the time these words were written down, which fits the book being gathered after Jerusalem fell. The Greek translation lacks it (see the note at 1:1; this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); a hissing (L), an object of scorn (B), something people mock (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for *sar* and for this list. Readable supplies "drank it" and "It made them" to keep the list in short sentences.

decisions.choice: "princes" (L); "chefs" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Sar as 2 Kings 24:12-14 in French.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh king of Egypt: Pharaoh Neco, the king of that time
decisions.reason: In 605 BC the pharaoh was Neco II, who had killed Josiah (2 Kings 23:29) and whose army Nebuchadrezzar defeated that year at Carchemish (46:2). Egypt heads the foreign nations, from the south, and the list moves north and east to Babylon at the end.

decisions.choice: his servants and his princes: the members of his court and his high officials
decisions.reason: "Servants" here are a king's courtiers and officials, not household slaves.

decisions.choice: servants and princes (L); servants and officials (B); officials and leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for a king's servants and for *sar*. Balanced keeps "servants" so that the two words stay distinct.

vi.L: mọi dân tạp chủng, mọi vua của xứ Út-xơ, mọi vua của xứ Phi-li-tin: Ách-ca-lôn, Ga-xa, Éc-rôn và những người sót lại của Ách-đốt;

ko.L: 그리고 모든 섞여 사는 백성과, 우스 땅의 모든 왕과, 블레셋 사람들의 땅의 모든 왕, 곧 아스글론과 가사와 에그론과 아스돗의 남은 자들,
ko.B: 그곳에 섞여 사는 모든 이방 백성, 우스 땅의 모든 왕, 블레셋 땅의 모든 왕, 곧 아스글론과 가사와 에그론과 아스돗의 남은 사람들,
ko.R: 이집트에 섞여 살던 외국 사람들도 모두 마셨다. 우스 땅의 모든 왕도 마셨다. 블레셋 땅의 모든 왕, 곧 아스글론과 가사와 에그론의 왕들과 아스돗에 남은 사람들도 마셨다.

decisions.choice: the mixed people: foreigners living among the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The word means a mixture of peoples. With Egypt it most likely means the foreign groups settled there, such as hired soldiers and traders (compare 50:37; Exodus 12:38, where the same word is used of the mixed crowd leaving Egypt).

decisions.choice: the land of Uz: a region east or south-east of Judah, near Edom
decisions.reason: Uz is the homeland of Job (Job 1:1). Lamentations 4:21 links it with Edom, and Genesis 36:28 lists Uz among the descendants of Seir in Edom.

decisions.choice: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod: the Philistine cities that still stood
decisions.reason: Gath, the fifth Philistine city, is missing; it had lost its importance long before (Amos 6:2). Ashdod is called a "remnant" because it had been badly weakened by war, in particular a long Egyptian siege in the seventh century BC (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: all the foreign peoples there (B); all the foreigners who lived in Egypt (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that this group belongs with Egypt (m1). Readable supplies "So did" and "the cities of".

decisions.choice: "Út-xơ, Ách-ca-lôn, Ga-xa, Éc-rôn, Ách-đốt"
decisions.reason: The published forms of these names (1 Chronicles 1:17; 1 Samuel 5-6; 2 Samuel 1:20), used through the list of verses 18-26.

decisions.choice: "우스", "블레셋", "아스글론", "가사", "에그론", "아스돗"
decisions.reason: Published Korean forms of these names (Genesis, Samuel, Kings).

decisions.choice: Edom, Moab and Ammon: Judah's neighbors to the south-east and east, across the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The three are often named together as Judah's kin and rivals (9:25; 27:3). Jeremiah gives each its own oracle in chapters 48-49.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: As in 9:25, "sons of Ammon" is the people of Ammon. Literal keeps the Hebrew form with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Zimri: an unknown people

decisions.choice: Elam and Media: kingdoms east of Babylon, in what is now Iran
decisions.reason: Elam lay east of Babylonia (49:34-39). Media lay to the north-east; the Medes later joined in the attack on Babylon (51:11, 28). The list now reaches the far east of the known world.

decisions.choice: Sheshach: a coded name for Babylon
decisions.reason: Sheshach is Babylon written in a simple code called *atbash*, in which the first letter of the alphabet stands for the last, the second for the next to last, and so on. By that code the consonants of Babel become those of Sheshach. In 51:41 Sheshach stands in parallel with Babylon, which confirms the meaning, and 51:1 uses the same code for the Chaldeans. Since Babylon is named openly elsewhere, the code was probably not for secrecy; it may be a play on words or a mark of contempt. The Greek translation lacks this sentence (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: will drink after them: the king of Babylon, God's instrument, will drink the cup last
decisions.reason: The nations Babylon conquers drink first; then Babylon itself must drink, as verses 12-14 have said. The verb changes from past to future: the list of those who drank ends with what will still happen.

decisions.choice: each to his brother: one after another
decisions.reason: The idiom means each in turn, one following the next.

decisions.choice: the king of Sheshach, that is, Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and adds what it stands for, since most readers would not recognize the code (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the name alone, with the footnote.
